claims.quote: Snowman / figure of 8 CXR Supracardiac TAPVR

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Cardiac: CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour
claims.quote: C - Cardiac: CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour; valves; pacemaker leads.

claims.text: Supracardiac TAPVR: the anomalous venous pathway creates a second round shadow above the heart, often likened to a snowman
claims.quote: In supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return, the anomalous venous pathway creates a second round shadow above the heart, often likened to the appearance of a snowman.

claims.text: With pulmonary venous obstruction: small heart and severe diffuse pulmonary edema; otherwise cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascular markings
claims.quote: Chest x-ray shows a small heart and severe diffuse pulmonary edema when there is pulmonary venous obstruction; otherwise, there is cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascular markings.

claims.text: Causes The pulmonary veins drain to a confluence behind the left atrium but do not connect to it; all pulmonary venous return enters the systemic venous circulation, and systemic flow depends on an adequate atrial communication (PFO or ASD)
claims.quote: In total anomalous pulmonary venous return, the pulmonary veins drain to a confluence adjacent to the posterior wall of the left atrium but do not connect to the left atrium. Instead, the entire pulmonary venous return enters the systemic venous circulation through one or more persistent embryologic connections. Filling of the left heart structures and systemic blood flow is dependent on having an adequate atrial communication (stretched patent foramen ovale or actual atrial septal defect).

claims.text: The infradiaphragmatic type is invariably severely obstructed (dramatic pulmonary edema and cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen soon after birth); the other 2 types typically are not obstructed
claims.quote: The infradiaphragmatic drainage type is invariably severely obstructed, leading to dramatic pulmonary edema and cyanosis unresponsive to supplemental oxygen that manifest shortly after birth. The other 2 types do not typically involve obstruction and lead to mild to moderate signs of heart failure and mild cyanosis in the first month of life.

claims.text: Symptoms Obstructed: respiratory distress, pulmonary edema and marked cyanosis; exam usually shows a parasternal lift and a single, loud S2 with no significant murmur
claims.quote: Neonates with obstructed pulmonary venous return present with respiratory distress, pulmonary edema, and marked cyanosis. Physical examination usually shows a parasternal lift and a single, loud second heart sound (S2), with no significant murmur.

claims.text: Unobstructed: mild heart failure symptoms may be present; some infants with supracardiac or cardiac types are asymptomatic
claims.quote: If pulmonary venous return is not obstructed, mild symptoms of heart failure may be present. Some infants with unobstructed supracardiac or cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return may be asymptomatic.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: emergent surgical repair
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Pediatric / Congenital CXR Signs table

claims.text: Obstructed TAPVR needs emergent surgical repair; in older infants, treat heart failure, then repair once stabilized
claims.quote: Neonates with total anomalous pulmonary venous return with obstruction require emergent surgical repair. In older infants, heart failure should be treated, followed by surgical repair as soon as the infant is stabilized.

claims.text: Repair: a wide anastomosis between the pulmonary venous confluence and the posterior wall of the left atrium, with ligation of the vein decompressing the confluence
claims.quote: Surgical repair consists of creating a wide anastomosis between the pulmonary venous confluence and the posterior wall of the left atrium. Ligation of the vein decompressing the confluence into the systemic venous circulation is important to prevent a postoperative left-to-right shunt.
